races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Something Coming
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse from the Peter Chapple-Hyam stable, ridden by Olivia Tubb; ran creditably at 7f on Standard AW twice (two placed efforts from five similar-going runs) but needs a strong pace to produce a late charge, which looks unlikely with Bundok unchallenged up front.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts, Something Coming nevertheless brings a second two runs back and solid fitness after 23 days off, with experience over today's trip and conditions and a handy draw from stall one working in her favour.

runners_data.name: Bundok
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's 82-day absentee steps up to 7f after running in 6f contests and is racing beyond its usual trip; Alfie Redman (5lb claim) takes the ride, and while the horse is the confirmed pace-setter its lone comparable AW Standard run produced only a fifth — that absence and step up in trip temper expectations despite its tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Bundok has posted consecutive thirds in her last two starts and shaped with enough promise to earn a top ranking here, with distance and going experience lending further confidence; the main concern is a layoff of 82 days without a win to her name.

runners_data.name: Unionville
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's three-year-old returns quickly (14 days) and has placed twice at 7f on Standard AW going from ten attempts; Owen Lewis claims 3lb, the hold-up style is genuine, and the horse needs a contested gallop to deliver — one win from ten similar-going runs suggests a need for everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Unionville arrives here on the back of a third two starts back, returning fit on a 14-day turnaround with both distance and going experience in his favour, and 138 lb is the main query against him going one better.

runners_data.name: Musical Soldier
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's in-form performer carries tongue-tie and arrives on the back of three wins in its last six starts (9/15 on similar going), and the prominent style maps perfectly onto this race shape with Bundok likely to set a manageable pace just ahead; the 1-day turnaround from its last run is the principal concern, though the form is compelling.
runners_data.comment: Musical Soldier won three times in his last six starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a run just one day ago raises freshness concerns, and he steps in at 138 lb having finished second most recently.

runners_data.name: Viviana
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's hold-up filly has been active (14 days since last run) and carries a 4/36 trainer-14 record; though placed in midfield on the pace map, she is a genuine hold-up type who will ideally want to be closer to the rear than the map shows, and her solitary comparable AW Standard run produced a seventh — the style mismatch works against her here.
runners_data.comment: Viviana shaped with real promise when a close second two starts back, and her experience over today's trip plus a rating that edges above her official mark suggest she is better than her mark implies; the concern is a winless run of six recent starts.

runners_data.name: Chapman's Peak
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's three-year-old wears a hood and has two placed efforts from ten runs, with recent form showing a slide (7th, 8th, 8th, 4th, 2nd); a genuine hold-up performer who has been pushed into a midfield position by the congestion of similar-styled horses, and the drop to 7f from 8f may help but the AW Standard form is thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Chapman's Peak at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a return to form two starts back offers a flicker of hope, though his overall profile from draw 7 off 134 lb suggests a midfield battle at best.

runners_data.name: Orange Emperor
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's hold-up horse is fitted with a hood/pads combination and returns in 17 days with one placed effort from ten AW Standard runs; Donagh Murphy (3lb claim) rides, and while a second at 7f on Good ground hints at ability, the horse is placed out of its natural rear position by this field's composition, diluting any finishing threat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Orange Emperor faces a stiff ask here; a third three starts back offers the sole bright spot, and he has run over today's trip and going, returning after 17 days off from stall three.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' visor-wearing hold-up runner is OR 52 — the lowest-rated horse in the field — and returned from a break nine days ago; though it has two wins in its recent form string (7f Good ground), those came on going that does not mirror tonight's Standard-to-Slow AW surface, and its natural position at the rear of the field will make winning from this pace map very difficult.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Superstorm is hard to fancy at these weights, though he did win two starts back and a second last time out shows he retains some form; he has run over today's trip and going before, and nine days ago is a perfectly fresh return.

races.paceDynamic: Bundok is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 7f Kempton AW heat and, with no serious challenger for the lead, should bowl along at a sustainable gallop without being harassed — a controlled, single-pace race is the most likely shape. Musical Soldier is a genuine prominent type and will look to sit just off Bundok's shoulder, giving the leader company but not a true duel. The remainder of the field — Something Coming, Viviana, Chapman's Peak, Orange Emperor, Superstorm, and Unionville — are natural hold-up horses, but the field contains far more of them than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Viviana, Chapman's Peak and Orange Emperor are the most likely to be shuffled forward into midfield against their instincts rather than settling in their true position. A steady-to-moderate pace set by a lone front-runner on a flat, right-handed polytrack favours horses racing prominently or from just off the pace who can quicken into the straight — pure hold-up horses will find the tempo insufficient to set up the late surge they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bundok Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Bundok is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a measured, even tempo that suits the horse in behind rather than the closers.
scenarios.body: Bundok rolls along in front with Musical Soldier tracking closely, and the moderate gallop means stamina reserves are intact turning in, rewarding the horse that can quicken soonest from a handy position; hold-up horses simply cannot generate enough momentum from the rear to reel in front-runners on a flat track with limited pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Soldier presses Bundok hard enough to force a genuine gallop and the pair pull clear of a tightly-bunched midfield pack.
scenarios.body: A true contested pace would stretch the field early and expose the hold-up horses who are already out of their natural positions, but Musical Soldier's excellent recent form (three wins in last five) makes this a realistic secondary shape with a horse well-placed to benefit from any tiring leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely fast enough to soften the front two and a horse from just off the pace produces a strong late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Viviana, Chapman's Peak or Orange Emperor to travel smoothly in what would be an artificially compressed midfield, then deliver a sustained finish — plausible only if a stronger-than-expected gallop is set; all three carry STYLE_FIT discounts as natural hold-up horses racing out of role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Off Race
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses sharply in the straight and a trailing horse swoops from the back of the field.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the flat, speed-friendly Kempton AW configuration and a single front-runner unlikely to set a scorching pace; Something Coming and Superstorm would need an improbable late sprint for this to materialise, and Superstorm's headgear (visor) adds further uncertainty over its reliability.

watchPoints.text: Musical Soldier is a genuine danger to all: three wins in last six, a style that maps directly onto the pace shape, and a 1-day turnaround is the only flag — watch if it travels easily behind Bundok turning in.

Bundok's 82-day absence and step up from 6f to 7f are unproven quantities; if the horse fails to stride clear early or ties up in the final furlong, the whole pace map collapses and the race opens up for whoever is closest to the front.

Viviana, Chapman's Peak and Orange Emperor are all genuine hold-up types squeezed into midfield positions — watch the early stages to see if any drift back to their natural berth, as a congested midfield with misplaced horses could cause trouble at a crucial stage of the race.

The going is confirmed Standard to Slow throughout the card, which adds a small stamina premium for the 7f trip — horses with proven AW form (Musical Soldier, Something Coming, Unionville) gain a marginal edge over those whose placed form came on Good turf.

The apprentice claiming context matters: Libby Swallow (7lb) on Musical Soldier delivers the biggest weight relief in the field — on an OR of 61 that claim is significant and inflates the horse's competitive weight-adjusted profile relative to rivals carrying fewer or no claims.

races.name: Unibet More Extra Place Races Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)
Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day/ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Al Widyan
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's well-regarded colt showed ability on debut at Goodwood (4th/6f) and William Buick takes the ride, but his natural hold-up style means he will likely be pushed closer to midfield in this congested field, tempering confidence in a big late swoop.

runners_data.name: Asgar
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's two-year-old has placed twice at 6f including on soft ground, and a prominent racing style suits this test well; the 87-day absence is worth noting but Cox sends runners back fit.

runners_data.name: Blue Victory
runners_data.note: William Knight's colt was only fifth on Goodwood debut but switches to AW for the first time; a hold-up style on a track that will likely reward prominent horses is a tactical negative to factor in.

runners_data.name: Coatimundi
runners_data.note: Charles Hills representative shows a hold-up tendency and carries a fades-in-finish flag from previous form; on a Standard to Slow surface that stretches stamina, that profile looks vulnerable over this 6f trip.

runners_data.name: Farasan
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this Gosden runner who was sixth over 7f at Goodwood last time; drops back to 6f here and the hold-up style means Murphy will need to produce a powerful run through horses on a surface where gaps are not guaranteed.

runners_data.name: I Am Royal
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unknown-style runner for Richard Hughes, recording a third on Goodwood debut nine days ago; freshness is a mild concern but Billy Loughnane's claim may be a factor, and the unknown style means this runner could slot anywhere in the field.

runners_data.name: Stormy Winter
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, Saeed bin Suroor's filly can take an uncontested lead under Cieren Fallon; both runs came over 7f at Goodwood, so the drop to 6f on a different surface introduces some unknowns, but the pace advantage here is significant.

runners_data.name: Agent Rose
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' filly holds a genuine hold-up profile but is mapped closer to midfield given the field's composition; her sole similar-going effort returned a seventh over 7f AW, and an 84-day absence combined with a positional compromise weakens her claims considerably.

runners_data.name: Love Always
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's debutante with unknown going and an absent last-run figure; completely unexposed and the unknown style means she could race anywhere — pure speculation at this point with no historical data to anchor an assessment.

runners_data.name: Sierra Belle
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly is the form horse of the field with two consecutive seconds over 6f at Goodwood, and Rossa Ryan's booking is a positive; a prominent style suits the likely race shape ideally, making her profile one of the cleanest fits in the field.

runners_data.name: Snow On The Beach
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for James Owen who has placed form over 6f on Standard and Fibresand, so the AW surface is familiar; 0W0P on similar going is a slight flag but the tactical profile fits reasonably well if the pace is moderate.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Progress
runners_data.note: Daisy Hitchins' runner carries a fades-in-finish warning and has finished 11th and 13th in both AW starts; hold-up style on a surface where she has no wins or places from two attempts paints a difficult picture.

races.paceDynamic: Stormy Winter is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner novice and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Cieren Fallon can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on what is effectively a Standard to Slow surface at Kempton's 6f AW straight. The pace will be honest but not brutal — a lone leader setting their own rhythm over six furlongs on this track typically produces a thorough test of finishing speed rather than a truly searching gallop, meaning the lead becomes a prime tactical asset. Al Widyan and Agent Rose are genuine hold-up horses by nature but, with the field carrying more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear, both are likely to find themselves racing closer to midfield than their natural position suggests, softening any late-closing threat they might otherwise pose. This race shape firmly favours horses who can race prominently or press the pace from a handy position, as Stormy Winter's uncontested lead will set a tempo that suits those tracking within two or three lengths, giving them first run on the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stormy Winter controls
scenarios.trigger: If Stormy Winter bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but not excessive pace, dictating throughout.
scenarios.body: Cieren Fallon gets a soft lead and controls every yard, arriving at the furlong pole full of running; horses tracking prominently get the clearest passage into the straight and first crack at the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent racer pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent horse tracks Stormy Winter within two lengths and produces a strong finishing kick.
scenarios.body: The leader is caught late by a horse who has enjoyed the ideal stalking position, with the Standard to Slow surface ensuring the mid-race tempo is not quick enough to expose the leaders early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, closers run on
scenarios.trigger: If Stormy Winter sets a stronger pace than expected and ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Horses from midfield who travel smoothly then get a run down the rail or wide could mop up, but this scenario is tempered by the fact that Al Widyan and Agent Rose — the truest hold-up types — are likely mapped closer to midfield and may not find their natural late gear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic early pace
scenarios.trigger: If rivals attempt to challenge Stormy Winter for the lead, creating a contested and faster-than-expected early gallop.
scenarios.body: The pace dynamic breaks down with multiple horses vying for position in the first two furlongs, leaving all front-runners exposed; a horse that drops back from a prominent position and delivers a sustained run through the field would benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Stormy Winter's early lead is the race's defining tactical factor — watch whether any rival challenges her for the front in the opening furlong, as any pressure could materially change the outcome.

Sierra Belle is the most prominently styled, in-form runner in the field; watch how quickly Rossa Ryan positions her behind the leader, as anything beyond three lengths off the pace may cost her the winning advantage.

Al Widyan and Agent Rose are genuine hold-up horses who will likely race closer to midfield than their natural style dictates — watch whether they find a clear run down the straight or get boxed in behind the pack.

The going is officially Standard to Slow throughout tonight's card, which is slower than the Goodwood Good ground most runners have experienced — watch for any horse who lacks the necessary stride pattern to handle the slower AW surface.
Love Always debuts with no form data and unknown style; watch for unexpected early speed or a wide draw that could disrupt the projected pace map in the first two furlongs.

races.name: Unibet/ebf Novice Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Anchor
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Clare Hobson who has shown zero wins and zero places in its last two visible runs, both at similar trips and going; 28 days between runs is routine, but its form figure of 0 and a history showing just one placing from two recent AW starts offers little encouragement that it can launch a winning late run without a genuine pace to chase.|

runners_data.name: Fortitudine
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby and William Buick land the strongest trainer-jockey combination in the race, and Fortitudine's sole career start — a win over 11f on Standard AW — maps perfectly onto tonight's conditions and distance; a 28-day freshener, 3-year-old lightly raced profile, and natural prominent style in a race with only one true pace-setter puts it in the prime tactical position.|

runners_data.name: No Ordinary Joe
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran whose most recent form figure is 9, who fades in finishes (tagged), and whose one win at similar going came at 20f — well beyond tonight's 1m3f — making it hard to see how it competes off the pace without a truly exhausting gallop that this field is unlikely to produce.|

runners_data.name: Shadow Road
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over this course and distance on Standard going last time, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) reflects that tonight's field pushes it into a role slightly out of character — though in this case it IS the natural leader; John Butler's runner is most likely to secure the rail, but if pressed it may run below its best.|

runners_data.name: Brave Hunter
runners_data.note: A visor-wearing, genuinely prominent-natured 3-year-old whose trainer form over 14 days is modest (1/4), and who faces a 55-day absence returning on AW for the first time in its recent form string — its natural desire to race up with the pace is constrained here because Shadow Road and Fortitudine are already ahead of it in the order, meaning it will need things to go wrong in front to get competitive.|

runners_data.name: Roxy Power
runners_data.note: The Crisford-trained 3-year-old is entirely unknown going — tagged UNKNOWN — with no days-since-last-run figure and no accessible form string, making it a genuine wildcard; Silvestre De Sousa rides for a yard in good 14-day form (2/20) but the lightly raced flag and style tagged U mean this horse's behaviour in the race is the most unpredictable factor in the field.|

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Road is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a six-runner field over 1m3f at Kempton AW, the early fractions are likely to be measured and controlled rather than pressured. Fortitudine, though mapped as prominent, will sit just off Shadow Road's shoulder, creating a conventional, compressed lead group with the rest — Anchor, No Ordinary Joe, and Brave Hunter — tracking further back. The Standard to Slow surface at Kempton tonight will stretch stamina in the home straight, rewarding horses that travel smoothly through the race rather than those who expend energy fighting for position early. This race shape strongly favours a prominent runner who can latch onto Shadow Road's sustainable gallop and produce a clean, decisive finish — a hold-up horse launching from deep will need a strong enough tempo to have been softened up, which one controlled front-runner is unlikely to generate. Brave Hunter is a genuine prominent type pushed into a midfield map position because Fortitudine and Shadow Road are already filling the prominent slots ahead of it; Shadow Road is most likely to actually secure the rail and front-running berth, with Fortitudine best placed to lock in second position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Road dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the race sets up for the horse tracking closest.
scenarios.body: Shadow Road rolls along at a sustainable clip, allowing Fortitudine to travel just off the pace in a rhythm-perfect position before asserting in the final furlong; Kempton's flat AW surface and Standard to Slow going reward exactly this style of prominent, patient racing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Road's recent course-and-distance win translates into an unassailable lead that none can reel in.
scenarios.body: Shadow Road, last seen winning over this C&D on Standard going, sets a pace so comfortable in front that no rival can close the gap in the straight; the Standard to Slow conditions limit the closing kick of hold-up horses, allowing the leader to bank stamina and sprint clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the hold-up horses get an unexpectedly strong tempo to run into.
scenarios.body: Anchor or Roxy Power would need Shadow Road to seriously misfire or a tactical incident to generate the kind of end-to-end gallop that brings them into play; given one dominant pace-setter and a slow surface, this is the least intuitive shape for this field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Order Disrupted
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Road dwells, refuses to lead, or the field bunches and produces an untidy tactical race.
scenarios.body: A scrambled pace would open the race up to Brave Hunter, whose genuine prominence means it could seize a forward position if the early order breaks down; No Ordinary Joe, despite its age and declining form, has won at 20f and could benefit from an unusually slow, compressed race that turns into an endurance test.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Road (front-runner) — if it is allowed to roll along unchallenged at a comfortable clip, the race shape locks in immediately; watch whether anything attempts to harry it in the first half-mile, because if nothing does, the race is effectively set.
Fortitudine — William Buick will dictate when and how hard he presses Shadow Road; if Buick moves early into the straight, the race could be over quickly and runners further back will have no answer.

Brave Hunter — returning after 55 days with a visor, a natural front-runner squeezed back in the order; watch for it pulling hard or failing to settle if it cannot secure its preferred position behind the leader.

Roxy Power — unknown profile and no visible last-run date means it is the one runner who could produce an unexpected pace injection or behavioural quirk that disrupts the settled rhythm Shadow Road is trying to create.

No Ordinary Joe — at 10 years old and finishing last on its most recent run, monitor whether it is even competitive early; if it drops out tamely, the field effectively becomes five runners and the pace dynamic tightens further around Fortitudine and Shadow Road.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Smartview Racecards Fillies' Handicap Stakes (London Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner trained by Ed Dunlop; has gate speed and five recent starts on Good ground, returning to a synthetic surface where similar-going form is limited (5 runs, 0W 2P), so the AW surface is a mild query despite the flat draw advantage.|
runners_data.comment: Zoustar Dreams won three starts back and has since posted consecutive fourths, though she returns fit on 19 days' rest with distance and going experience and a featherweight draw from stall one; the risk is reproducing that winning form after a dip in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Got The Booty
runners_data.note: Returns after a 79-day absence for Clive Cox, who has a 3/21 14-day strike rate; was runner-up twice on AW at this trip and goes fresh, but the layoff combined with the need to fight for the lead from the outset represents a notable fitness risk.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Got The Booty at least showed consistency with two seconds and a third before that ninth last time out, though 79 days off adds a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going, but faces a stiff task from stall six carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Just Queen High
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on this 4yo hold-up filly; her recent form on Good and Soft ground shows multiple weak finishes, but she won on Heathcoat AW (similar all-weather pace) and her 1W from 9 similar-going runs suggests she needs things to fall right tactically.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a winner in her last five starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making Just Queen High an interesting contender returning after 63 days; the recent string of unplaced efforts demands respect, but she carries 137 lb from stall eight on a mark of 67.

runners_data.name: Amelia's Joy
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-racing 4yo who has won twice and placed three times from 15 similar-going starts; David Probert reunites with her and she arrives in good nick (16 days), wearing headgear (p) that has featured in her recent better runs — her course form and strike rate make her highly relevant.|
runners_data.comment: Amelia's Joy brings a win and a third in her last six starts, and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, making her a solid each-way contender at 136 lb from stall four; the worry is that seventh on her most recent outing leaves a question mark over current form.

runners_data.name: Egotistical
runners_data.note: Roger Varian 3yo prominent-style filly with a win on Good 6f ground; has been placed three times from seven similar-going runs, including a recent 2nd over this exact course-and-distance on Standard, which represents strong course-and-distance suitability from just off the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Egotistical shaped well when runner-up last time out and has run over today's trip, with our rating of 78 marking her out as the one to beat in this field; the risk is that she has finished fourth and seventh in her two starts before that.

runners_data.name: Startled Lady
runners_data.note: William Knight's 3yo has won over 6f Good and placed twice from 12 similar-going outings; prominent style suits a contested pace and she is 32 days fresh — her 6f Goodwood win and course experience make her a player if she secures a clean prominent pitch.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Startled Lady makes this assignment look tough, and her eighth last time out — following a win two starts back — does little to build confidence; she has run over today's trip and returns after 32 days, but there is limited reason to get excited.

runners_data.name: Remi Mae
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo hold-up filly is ridden by Oisin Murphy, who rarely wastes a booking; headgear (t) worn and has placed three times from seven similar-going efforts including a second over 6f Standard — arrives 21 days fresh and will want the pace to be honest to make her late run count.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Remi Mae is hard to fancy despite routinely hitting the frame — three thirds and a disqualified effort among those runs suggest she finds one too good; experience over today's trip is some small consolation.

runners_data.name: Overbudget
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 3yo has a genuine prominent running style but, with two confirmed front-runners and multiple prominent types in this field, she is realistically unlikely to secure her natural position and may find herself racing further back than ideal, which reduces her chance of producing her best form given her limited all-weather strike rate.|

races.paceDynamic: Zoustar Dreams and Got The Booty are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 6f Kempton AW trip, creating a genuinely competitive early pace rather than an uncontested gallop. Zoustar Dreams has the stronger lead-from-the-front profile with gate speed on turf-equivalent surfaces, while Got The Booty — returning after 79 days — will press hard on her outside, ensuring the tempo is honest to strong throughout. Prominent types Amelia's Joy, Egotistical, and Startled Lady will be racing for positions just off the pace, with the field holding more forward-biased runners than can all secure their natural spot, meaning Overbudget — a genuine prominent racer — is most likely to be shuffled back further than ideal. This shape — contested pace, honest gallop, tight bend into the straight — favours hold-up runners and closers who travel smoothly behind the speed, with Remi Mae and Just Queen High best placed to exploit tired leaders late, provided they can find clear running on the home turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Zoustar Dreams and Got The Booty burn each other up setting a strong early tempo and the prominent trio cannot all get cover.
scenarios.body: The two leaders press on briskly through the first three furlongs, creating a strong gallop that strings the field out and leaves the pace-setters vulnerable in the final furlong; hold-up horses who have been able to travel smoothly behind the speed then pick up the pieces on the run to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lead Pair Dominate Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace settles rather than burns and one of the two front-runners establishes a comfortable lead without expending excess energy.
scenarios.body: Zoustar Dreams or Got The Booty controls proceedings from the front without being truly pressured in the middle section, conserving enough for the final furlong; prominent runners cannot close the gap given the Standard To Slow surface adding just enough cut to reward a relaxed front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Take Advantage
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders race each other into the ground early and the hold-up horses fail to find a clear run on the home turn, leaving prominent types to capitalise from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Amelia's Joy or Egotistical settle in the slipstream of the leaders through the first half, switch off the pace smoothly and have a decisive positional advantage over the hold-up horses when the front pair tire; the Standard To Slow surface limits the ability of horses coming from the back to make up ground in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches significantly on the home turn, causing interference that disrupts the fancied hold-up runners and creates a chaotic final furlong.
scenarios.body: Remi Mae or Just Queen High are hampered or must switch wide, nullifying their late-run advantage and handing the race to a horse that avoids trouble cleanly; Startled Lady, who won over this course-and-distance configuration, benefits from her tactical versatility if she secures a clear passage.

watchPoints.text: Zoustar Dreams and Got The Booty both want to lead — watch the first furlong for a fierce duel that could burn them both out and set up the race for hold-up horses.
Got The Booty returns after 79 days and must fight for the lead immediately; monitor her in the parade ring for signs of peak condition before committing to her front-running claims.

Overbudget is a natural prominent-style runner but has nowhere natural to go in this pace-rich field — watch to see if Mason Paetel (3) drops her in early or is forced wide, as either scenario compounds her chance.
Remi Mae (Oisin Murphy) will be delivered late off the home turn — watch her for clear-run issues on the bend, as Kempton's tight configuration can trap hold-up horses if the field fans wide.
Egotistical's recent second over this exact 6f AW course-and-distance for Roger Varian (5/16 14-day) makes her a significant one to monitor as a course specialist with proven Standard-going form.

races.name: Unibet Supporting Safer Gambling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Aigeas
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up operator whose best recent effort was a win over 6f on Standard — the step up to 7f here is a mild concern, and Mason Paetel's 3lb claim helps offset the weight; ran 7 days ago so freshness is fine, and similar-going form reads two wins from six efforts.
runners_data.comment: Aigeas won two starts back and returns on a quick turnaround of just seven days, bringing both distance and going experience to the table; the main concern is that his most recent run was a ninth, leaving something to prove on that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sands
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride for Ed Dunlop who is 2/19 in the past fortnight — a yard in solid form — and Sierra Sands brings back-to-back wins over 7f at Goodwood, making this trip and a prominent position his comfort zone; 32 days off is not a concern given the trainer's current strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Sierra Sands won back-to-back two and three starts back, has run over today's trip, and returns 32 days after his latest outing — his 87 rating underlines his credentials as a leading threat, though the fourth last time out raises a question about his latest form.

runners_data.name: Shaman Champion
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners this Clive Cox-trained 3yo who steps back to 7f after showing a placed effort over this trip on Standard in his history; the form string of 2-7003 is modest and only one placed run in ten efforts on similar going limits confidence, though Cox is 3/21 in the past 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a second five starts back, Shaman Champion heads this field on our rating and shaped encouragingly on his latest outing 37 days ago; winless in recent starts, but his experience over today's trip and a weight of 134 lb from stall 6 make him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Raggaas
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell and the Crisford team (2/20 in 14 days) combine on this progressive 3yo who won over 7f at Goodwood last time and whose form has been building consistently; stepping back in trip from middle distances could sharpen a turn of foot that has been slightly blunted at longer distances.
runners_data.comment: Raggaas won last time and has run over today's trip, but our figures rank him last of eight in this field, making him difficult to fancy on ratings grounds despite his recent course to form.

runners_data.name: Comic Hero
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is the standout jockey booking and Balding's strike rate (13/64 in 14 days) is strong, but Comic Hero is a genuine prominent-style horse whose natural racing position will be unavailable in this traffic — its best form at 7f on AW came when getting an easy lead and the redistribution to midfield is a real disadvantage here.
runners_data.comment: Comic Hero showed a second two starts back and a win four starts back, so ability on a good day is clear, but a sixth last time out after 81 days off raises fitness questions; experience over today's trip and going helps, and 131 lb from stall 3 rounds out a mixed profile.

runners_data.name: Hardy's Hero
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon's front-running partnership with this William Haggas 3yo is the headline pace angle — Haggas is 9/49 in 14 days and Hardy's Hero has finished placed in five of his last five, consistently at 7f on Good or similar; the front-runner narrative hinges entirely on whether he can shake Manly Fireball off early.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Hardy's Hero faces a stiff task here despite consistent placing earlier in his recent form; he has run over today's trip and returns after 32 days, but the weight of 131 lb adds another hurdle.

runners_data.name: Manly Fireball
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane's mount for Richard Hughes brings a strong AW profile (8 of 9 runs on Polytrack/AW) and won over 6f on Standard in April — stepping to 7f is the trip question, but the horse has placed at the trip before; its prime role is as a pace-pressurer that may suit Hardy's Hero if it cannot sustain the duel.
runners_data.comment: Manly Fireball caught the eye with a runner-up finish last time out, and his win three starts back underlines he knows how to find the line; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 86 suggests he holds strong claims. The main risk is a burden of 129 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Blakefell
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa on a horse that ran just 9 days ago for Ivan Furtado (0/16 in 14 days — a cold trainer angle) — Blakefell has won over 7f on AW going and placed twice at Kempton's trip equivalent, but it is a naturally prominent horse whose racing style will be compressed into midfield by the sheer volume of pace in this field, reducing its chance of a clear passage.
runners_data.comment: Blakefell arrives here in decent nick after consecutive runner-up finishes, though a sixth four starts back tempers enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 86 gives him a fighting chance from stall 2 off 128 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Hardy's Hero and Manly Fireball are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested early gallop over this 7f Kempton AW trip on a Standard to Slow surface. Hardy's Hero has the more consistent profile at this trip and is likely to assert for the early rail position, with Manly Fireball pressing hard to his outside — the duel between them should generate an honest, pressured pace that stretches the field through the first three furlongs. Sierra Sands and Raggaas will push to be prominent just behind the speed, potentially crowding the front-running space and adding to early pressure. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure a natural position — Comic Hero and Blakefell are genuine prominent horses who will be shuffled back into midfield against their instincts, making the race harder to read from those positions; Hardy's Hero and Manly Fireball are the horses most likely to actually control the early race. With a contested lead and honest fractions on a surface that rewards those who travel smoothly into the race without expending energy in positional battles, this race shape most clearly favours prominent, forwardly-placed horses just off the speed who can draft into a pressured pace and pick off tiring leaders in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy's Hero and Manly Fireball fight for the lead and soften each other up, allowing a horse settled just off the pace to pounce.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners trade blows throughout, burning each other's reserves and leaving the race wide open in the final two furlongs for a prominent passenger to power through; Standard to Slow going rewards those who conserve energy early and finish strongly rather than those who expend it fighting for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners, most likely Hardy's Hero, controls the tempo and gets a soft lead without being seriously pressured.
scenarios.body: Hardy's Hero has repeatedly placed at 7f at this level and a race where the duel for the lead dissolves early — perhaps Manly Fireball being outpaced off the gate — could allow him to dictate and build an unassailable advantage; Cieren Fallon's intelligent front-running record gives this extra credibility.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly fierce and both front-runners wilt simultaneously, opening ground for a hold-up or redistributed prominent runner to finish through.
scenarios.body: Aigeas is the natural hold-up horse in the race and has won over 6f on Standard going before, suggesting a strong late kick is possible if the tempo creates enough of a gap; Comic Hero also has the engine to finish through beaten horses though its redistribution to midfield means it is racing against its natural instincts and may not get a clean run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Manly Fireball's presence disrupts Hardy's Hero's rhythm so severely that the race fragments into a chaotic finish with no one able to sustain a run.
scenarios.body: In a messy, stop-start 7f on a slower-than-advertised surface, fitness and adaptability become decisive and Blakefell — despite being mapped out of natural position — has course form and recently ran just 9 days ago suggesting peak fitness; Raggaas stepping back from middle-distance trips could find the compressed 7f finish playing to its advantage.

watchPoints.text: Hardy's Hero vs Manly Fireball — watch the first furlong for which front-runner asserts; if Hardy's Hero gets a clean jump and Manly Fireball is slow away, the leader scenario shifts from 22% to potentially race-decisive.

Comic Hero's draw and early traffic — Oisin Murphy will need to find a gap from an uncomfortable position for a horse that wants to be prominent; watch whether he tries to push forward early or accepts midfield, as either choice carries risk.

Blakefell's run style vs position — if Silvestre De Sousa chases position aggressively, it signals the horse is being forced to race against its map and could leave it weakened in the straight; a quiet, accepting start from Blakefell is the trigger for its late-race relevance.

Sierra Sands freshness — 32 days off but Dunlop is in form and the 7f trip is proven; watch market moves near post time as a well-supported Sierra Sands would validate the prominent-off-the-pace narrative as the dominant scenario.

Going surface creep — the going report shows Standard to Slow across all 7f races tonight, and if the surface is riding slower than headline Standard, hold-up horses like Aigeas gain marginal extra time to close, slightly elevating Scenario C probability in-running.

races.name: Bet £20 Get £20 With Unibet Handicap Stakes (London Middle Distance Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Joseph
runners_data.note: Has won at 10f on Standard AW and placed at 12f on the same surface — his sim-going record of 2 wins and 5 places from 15 is the most relevant in the field; headgear (p) fitted, David Egan rides, and 16 days since last run is a straightforward return for a horse whose hold-up style fits this tempo neatly.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner five starts back, Joseph returns after 16 days in good shape, with experience over today's trip and going and a rating of 74 working in his favour; the concern is whether he can rediscover that winning form after patchy recent efforts.

runners_data.name: Madjid
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 10f and 12f — most recently at Goodwood and Kempton — make the trip and surface credentials compelling; only 7 days since his last start is a slight query on freshness but trainer Harry Charlton's 14-day strike rate of 4/13 suggests confidence, and his natural hold-up style is well-suited to tracking Pershalla before unleashing a late effort.
runners_data.comment: Madjid arrives in the form of his life, winning back-to-back last time out and two starts back, and a swift seven-day turnaround suggests connections are keen to strike while he's hot. Has run over today's trip and tops the ratings here; 141 lb is the one query.

runners_data.name: Pershalla
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter who will enjoy an uncontested lead; she is racing out of her usual hold-up role (STYLE_FIT 0.94) and her sim-going record of 1 win from 13 on Standard is modest — the controlled tempo she sets benefits the field more than herself unless the gallop is genuinely slow from wire to wire.
runners_data.comment: Pershalla won last time out and arrives here just 16 days later in fine order, with experience of both today's trip and going working in her favour. The main risk is that her recent record beyond that victory has been inconsistent, with five finishes of fifth or worse before that win.

runners_data.name: Extraterrestrial
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose best form (two places on Standard AW over 10-11f) suggests ability, but 73 days off and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 confirm she is not operating from her natural position in this field — her chance depends on a pace scenario that may not materialise cleanly; Crisford yard running at 2/20 in the 14-day window adds further caution.

runners_data.name: Thatcham
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old arrives with only three runs on record, none beyond 10f, and the step to 1m3f on Standard To Slow is an untested combination — a true hold-up runner squeezed into a midfield slot, 20 days since last run, and no wins to date mean the profile asks many questions simultaneously.
runners_data.comment: Thatcham has experience of today's distance and going, and his rating of 68 suggests he holds genuine claims as a leading danger here, drawn four and carrying 129 lb; the chief concern is a trainer without a winner in 42 attempts over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Rogue Desire
runners_data.note: Longest absence in the field at 90 days; prominent-style runner (hg:t) whose four recorded runs show consistent mid-division finishes without threatening, and the step up to 1m3f at Kempton on Standard To Slow is uncharted territory — needs everything to improve sharply to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Rogue Desire has been off the track for 90 days and faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and draws stall one carrying 128 lb, but the overall profile makes her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Pershalla is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rivals to contest the lead, Cieren Fallon should be able to dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop around the Kempton polytrack over this 1m3f trip. The going report across all races on the card is Standard To Slow — marginally softer than the headline Standard — which will blunt raw speed and reward stamina-laden hold-up horses who can absorb a steadily-run contest before producing their finish. Extraterrestrial and Thatcham are genuine hold-up types redistributed into the midfield map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed; neither is likely to be as far back as their natural style demands, and the field holds more true closers than the map can honestly place at the rear. With Pershalla controlling from the front at a sustainable clip and a cluster of hold-up horses forced slightly closer than ideal, this race shape most favours a horse who can travel prominently or in close mid-division and then sustain a strong run through the final two furlongs — the profile that benefits is the hold-up/midfield horse with proven stamina at this trip and positive recent form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pershalla Dictates, Hold-Ups Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Pershalla leads unchallenged at a steady-to-fair tempo and the hold-up horses must produce their runs from midfield rather than a true last position.
scenarios.body: Pershalla sets a comfortable, controlled pace and the hold-up types — forced up closer than they'd like — have to use more energy in the middle of the race to maintain position, rewarding any horse that can travel smoothly in Pershalla's slipstream and quicken from a handy berth in the final quarter-mile. Joseph and Madjid, with genuine hold-up form and stamina over 10-12f on Standard surfaces, are the profiles best equipped to pick off a tiring front-runner in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Two Hold On
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely slow throughout and Pershalla, or any horse that travels prominently, simply outstays the field on the softer-than-ideal surface.
scenarios.body: A crawling gallop over 1m3f on a Standard To Slow surface can produce a muddling finish where those who conserve energy near the front outkick the hold-up horses who misjudge the pace; Pershalla and Rogue Desire, both suited to making their effort from a prominent berth, benefit most if no one gives chase until it is too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From True Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and genuine hold-up types can find clear running in the straight to deliver a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: Madjid has won over 10f and 12f on Standard going and arrives fresh off a 7-day turnaround in form; Joseph has a recent win at 10f on Standard and both carry enough stamina to finish powerfully if the race is truly run. However, this scenario is partially undermined because several tagged hold-up types are not operating from their true position, so the probability of a textbook late-finishing shape is reduced.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Take Over
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments into a ragged, stop-start contest where redistributed horses find gaps mid-race and grind their rivals down through stamina rather than any clean tactical move.
scenarios.body: Extraterrestrial has placed twice on Standard surfaces over 10-11f and Thatcham arrives lightly raced but with limited evidence at this trip and distance; both are racing out of their natural role in this shape, lowering the probability materially, but an unusually messy race could allow either to plug on through a tiring field.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Pershalla is allowed a completely uncontested lead from stall to home turn — if Cieren Fallon can find an unharrassed rhythm, the front-running scenario lengthens every hold-up horse's task markedly.

Joseph's headgear (p) is worth monitoring in the paddock and in the early stages; if he settles well for David Egan and tracks Pershalla from second or third, he is ideally positioned for the pace shape this race is likely to produce.

Madjid's 7-day turnaround is the shortest recovery in the field — if Lewis Edmunds is instructed to drop him out and produce a late run, note whether there is enough pace ahead to run on to, given how moderate the tempo may be.

Extraterrestrial's 73-day absence combined with her redistribution flag means Billy Loughnane may need to ride against her natural instincts to find a workable position — monitor whether she settles in mid-division or drops out wide and late, as the latter would make her task near-impossible.

The Standard To Slow going reading on the 1m3f trip (confirmed by the 7:00 race going report) is softer than the headline surface suggests — horses with proven stamina credentials on similar AW going should be prioritised over those whose best form came on Good turf.
